question_response: Dr. Kim clearly knows the subject deeply but struggles to communicate it in an accessible way for students at this level.
I appreciated Dr. Kim's enthusiasm for the material even when the lectures were hard to follow at times.
The course started strong but became increasingly disorganized in the second half of the semester. More structure is needed.
Dr. Kim made genuine efforts to be inclusive and regularly checked in with the class about pacing and understanding.
I felt uncomfortable during a few class discussions where certain perspectives were not handled with enough care or sensitivity.
The workload was unreasonably heavy for a three credit course. It was difficult to balance with my other responsibilities.
Dr. Kim was responsive to feedback midway through the semester and made real adjustments. I appreciated that willingness to adapt.
The grading took far too long. Waiting four weeks for assignment feedback made it impossible to learn from mistakes in time.
I needed more scaffolding on the major project. The expectations were unclear until very late in the process.
There should be alternative ways to demonstrate understanding beyond timed exams. Not all students perform equally under pressure.
The reading list was thoughtfully curated and included voices I had never encountered before. That was genuinely appreciated.
I had to miss several office hours because they were only offered during times that conflicted with my work schedule.
Dr. Kim should consider providing more low cost or free alternatives to the required course materials going forward.
